reasoning:
I judged on one lens only: would Alec be proud to post this on Instagram tomorrow? Near You wins clearly. Its first phone screen leads with a colour poster mosaic headed by the basketball image Alec himself praised. Its 'place' moments (a state outline with program dots in the results header, a real city-pin map, the location stamp on the hero) give the map wow he asked for without burying the sport art the way D did. Its grants screen is calm text, not repeated pictures. What holds it back is execution polish, not the concept: the floating Map pill covers content in nearly every screenshot, a state stamp clutters every card, names cut off on 2-up cards, and the heavy black bars pull away from white paper. All of these are fixable in one pass.

Clubhouse has the single most beautiful screen of the round, the sport community page with banner and avatar, plus the delightful coloured avatar grid. But its phone first screen is text only, it counts nationally everywhere (a voice violation), and its multi-sport hero is near-black.

Gallery's listing hero and share card are excellent and should be grafted onto Near You. Its feed fails the taste test: grey disabled sport bar, 16 identical tennis plates, 45 identical grant cards, and a place headline repeated under the same header. That is the vibe-coded repetition Alec will spot at once.

I did not average the scores: Near You 8, Clubhouse 6.5, Gallery 5. Screenshots read: /tmp/asnm-r3/{gallery,clubhouse,nearyou}/final-*.png.

reasoning:
I ran all three as Karen on a 390x844 phone in Playwright (ports 8811/8812/8813, all servers stopped by PID). Each prototype was tested with a fake Tampa GPS location, 9 typed variations of the place, a check of returning to results, and a tap-target and text-size audit. No concept passes every task, and each has at least one Karen-breaking defect.

What all three get wrong:
- Typing 'Tampa FL' with no comma fails everywhere ('We could not find'). So do 'St Pete', 'Saint Petersburg' and 'Brandon FL'.
- 'Use my location' snaps to 'Egypt Lake-Leto, FL', a name Karen won't recognize.
- Coming back from a listing drops her at the top of the list.
- Events is 2 taps to an honest empty page with Add an event, and the letter is about 2 taps plus typing. These are equal in all three.

Task by task:
- **Program near Tampa (3 taps in all three).** All show the same honest near ladder (4 in Tampa, 6 within about 25 mi). Clubhouse's compact rows and jump chips scan best. Gallery's cards are one per screen, so the page runs 9,883px. Near You cuts card names off and its Map pill covers text.
- **Basketball in Illinois (no data; Wisconsin has 2).** Clubhouse is broken: '31 listed so far / 0 cities / Nothing listed in Illinois yet', with no visible basketball filter. Near You is honest but stops there. Gallery is honest and offers somewhere to go, but its 'closest' list is really sorted by check date and leaves out Wisconsin.
- **Listing contact and trust.** All put Verified, 'Last checked' and a sticky Visit website on the first screen. Gallery's Back button works best. Clubhouse has no in-page Back. Near You's Back is javascript:history.back().
- **Grant for an athlete.** Gallery opens on athlete grants (3 taps). Clubhouse handles past deadlines best. Near You shows expired deadlines as live at the top of its list, an honesty failure against the opening-day grant bar.
- **'Use my location'.** It breaks Near You outright ('could not place'). It works in Clubhouse, and in Gallery after one extra tap.

Why Gallery wins: it has no dead end on any of the 6 tasks, the best grant and listing flows, a ZIP that resolves to a city name, and correct 'Use my location' distances. Its defects (the false 'closest' label, 'near' for 160 miles, long scroll, the 20px beta link) are fixable. Clubhouse's Illinois contradiction and Near You's broken 'Use my location' and live-looking expired grants hit Karen's core tasks directly.

Graft onto Gallery: Clubhouse's compact rows, jump chips and 'Grants open now' rail, and Near You's input on the home page, labeled 'near' distances and map.

strengths: Best fit for production. Hash routes already copy the real paths (#/sports/tennis, #/states/FL, #/programs/<id>, #/grants/<id>), so each one becomes a Worker route with its own meta. One 'community' template covers sport, state, grants and events, so the Worker needs one renderer for all four page types.

Most coherent design system. It has a real token set (--r-s/--r/--r-l/--r-xl = 8/12/16/20, which is the manual's radius scale exactly), a --font token with the manual's fallbacks, brand Ink, Graphite, Mist, Sand and Orange #C5430C, Teal for Verified, and few one-off sizes.

Compact 72px-plate rows keep pages short (Tampa phone page 3,934px, against D's 34,330), which suits server-rendered pages of 20 results. The big image appears once, in the banner and avatar, as the pattern brief asked.

Accessibility basics are in place: a skip link, a focus trap in the sheet and drawer with Escape and focus return, prefers-reduced-motion and forced-colors. Body text is 17px, the 44px tap targets were checked by script, and nothing scrolls sideways at 390px.

Honest near logic. All four groups are present (In Tampa 4 / within about 25 mi 6 / Elsewhere in Florida 69 / Florida, no city 30), and the empty states fall back to the whole state. The grant page handles a past deadline ('Last deadline June 15, 2026') and drops it from 'open now'. No email, phone, score or type field, and no money ask (grep and rendered text both clean). The official mark sits top-left, apart from the sport art.
weaknesses: axe found 4 violation types: (1) state tile map uses white on #8f8b83 at 3.39:1 with 10-12px text (6 nodes on phone, 12 on desktop); (2) aria-pressed on an <a> in the 'Verified only' chip (critical); (3) .banner has role=img with no accessible name; (4) .chiprow on /grants has a list role with <a> children (critical).

Counts the whole directory, which breaks voice.md and the pattern brief's 'counts only for the person's area' rule: '521 listed', '347 listed' and '134 listed' on the home avatar grid, and '347 listed so far · 345 checked by a person' on sport pages.
The letter copy promises emails the backend cannot send: 'We email when new tennis programs... show up near you', and 'Get the letter for Florida'. /api/subscribe stores no sport or place.

In-city matching is a word match, so 'Tennis Starts With Love · Tampa area, FL' counts as In Tampa. isPlaced only rejects 'statewide', so 'Raleigh / statewide, NC' still shows as a city on sport pages.
A sport page's Grants tab shows all 45 grants ('Grants 45' on Tennis), which suggests 45 tennis grants.
Program names keep en dashes ('City of Tampa Parks and Recreation – Wheelchair Tennis'), while grant names are rewritten to a colon. Pick one rule.

The home hero is type plus a search pill: the first phone screen shows no listing. The multi-sport house tone turns near-black on the listing hero, close to dark mode, and the faint second athlete behind the banner is busy for event, grant and multi.
mustFix: Fix the 4 axe failures: darken or label the tile-map low tier (or put ink text on a pale tile), replace aria-pressed on links with real buttons or aria-current, give the banner aria-hidden (the h1 already names the sport), and drop role=list from .chiprow or wrap each chip in an li.
Remove national totals from home and sport headers. Show counts only for the visitor's place or the state being viewed.
Make letter copy match /api/subscribe ('Get the letter'), or add sport and state fields to the subscribe schema first.
Use first-city parsing, as Near You's cityShort does, instead of a word match for 'In <city>'. Treat 'X / statewide' as statewide.
Filter the Grants tab by grant.sports when it is set, or label it 'Grants for any sport'.
Raise the tile map to 44px tiles or a list on phones.

strengths: Cleanest accessibility result: 0 axe WCAG 2.0/2.1/2.2 A and AA violations on all 22 routes scanned, phone and desktop. Sheet and overlay keep focus inside, return it on close, and close on Escape. reduced-motion and forced-colors are handled, and there is a real error message ('Enter an email address, like name@example.com.').

Strongest brand discipline. Orange #C5430C is kept to signals (the search button, the help link), Teal marks Verified, white paper with a Sand hero, DM Sans, and the official mark top-left and separate. It uses T8 two-tone plates and T3 inverted heroes exactly as the image lab specified, with OPT sizing.

Strictest placement rule: an UNPLACED regex (statewide, multiple, various, county, region) plus geoPrecision!=='state'. A ZIP resolves to its nearest gazetteer city, and in-city rows show no distance.

Best wow and share artifact: the 4:5 poster (white athlete on the sport's deep colour, name, City, ST, the domain, and the official logo in a white disc) maps directly to a server og:image built from <key>.png. The grant page leads with the amount and has a sticky 'Apply on their site' bar.
Grants list on a phone shows amount, audience and deadline on every card, which fixes the current spreadsheet view.
weaknesses: No skip link anywhere. The sport (#s=tennis), state (#st=FL) and grants (#v=grants) views render with no <h1>, which hurts both accessibility and SEO on exactly the pages that need to rank.
Routes are query-style hashes (#q=, #s=, #st=, #p=, #v=grants), not path mirrors. Each one needs remapping to /sports/:key, /states/:st and so on.

Text on the page claims more than it can show. 'Every listing says who checked it and when' is not true: no name is shown, and 236 rows have no date. Unverified pages say 'Not yet verified' next to 'Last checked October 9, 2026', which reads as a person checking and rejecting it. lastChecked is the automatic website check.

Dash handling is half done. Program names get ' – ' changed to ': ' (an official name altered), while grant names still show em dashes ('Triumph Foundation — Keep Moving Forward', 'Semper Fi / The Americas Fund — ...'). Its own QA claim 'dashes in names fixed' is false for grants.
The over-strict regex also unplaces 'Athens / Clarke County' and similar rows (77 placed rows with a county or region suffix), which loses real city distances.

The design system is thinner: tokens are colour plus one radius; radii vary (4/7/9/12/14/16/20/24); there are cqw-based type sizes; and card meta and trust text at 14-16px sit under the 17px body floor. The 29px tile-map tiles have 12px labels on phones.

The beta bar wraps to 2 lines on phones and the hero is about 310px, so no card shows on the first home screen. The desktop listing hero at 21:9 is heavy for pages that hold only trust and a description.
mustFix: Add a skip link and one h1 per view (sport, state, grants).
Replace 'who checked it' with 'Every listing says whether a person has checked it, and when'. Reword the unverified line to 'Listed <date>, not checked yet' (needs listedAt in /api/directory).
Pick one rule for dashes in names and apply it to programs and grants alike. Leaving data names verbatim is the more honest choice.
Parse the first city ('Athens / Clarke County' to Athens) before deciding a row is unplaced.

strengths: Most complete honest place logic and the only real map. In-city / about 25 mi / elsewhere in state by distance / statewide groups, with a state-outline results header (dots plus 'you' ring). MapLibre shows one pin per city with a count, and a 'Statewide in Florida · 30' strip that is never pinned. Wording is honest: 'Distances are city to city, so they are close, not exact'; 'Serves Florida, no single city listed'; 'Programs, placed at their city'.

cityShort reads the first city out of a list, which is better than either other concept's regex. State pages mix sports by turns (tennis, swimming, water skiing, soccer...), which cuts repeated pictures. ZIP search starts at about 25 mi.

Brand-correct colours (it uses --flame only as a token, never for text), Teal for Verified, the official mark top-left, a skip link, and counts only per place or state ('109 listings · 94 verified' in Florida).
weaknesses: Worst axe result: 16 color-contrast nodes on the home tile map (white on #E38A57 at 2.61:1, with 9-11px count text) and 9 on the sport tile map (#9a9792 on white at 2.91:1). Many sub-13px labels: tile counts at 9px, the 'Verified' card pill at 12.5px, the 'FL' stamp at 12px.

The floating Map pill sits over the card trust line (the date) on phone results and state pages. In the Tampa and Florida screenshots it hides 'checked Oct …'. The date is the opening-day bar, and the pill covers it.

Two-column phone cards cut off the city ('Atlantic Beac…', 'Palm Be…', 'Winter …') and the name after 2 lines ('City of Tampa Parks and…'). City and state are the only location we are allowed to show, and the layout drops them.
No focus trap in the sheet or drawer (Tab escapes, self-admitted). Uses alert() when location is missing. 200% zoom not tested.

The stamp on every card means inline state SVG paths per card. That adds server-rendered weight and repeats 'FL' on a page that is already about Florida. It also pushes the athlete down to about 54%, under the lab's 62%.
Routes are #near=, #s=, #st= hashes, not path mirrors. The design system is the loosest of the three: 15.5px, 12.5px and clamp(9px…) sizes, and radii of 4/7/10/12/14/18/20/22/24.
Grant names keep em dashes, and a deadline range shows 'Oct–Nov'.
mustFix: Fix tile-map contrast (ink on pale tiles, or darken to 4.5:1) and raise tile labels to 13px or more and tiles to 44px.
Move the Map pill so it never covers content (reserve bottom padding equal to the pill height plus safe area, or dock it in the results header). Never let it cover a date.
Use single-column cards or compact rows on phones so City, ST is never cut off.
Add a focus trap and replace alert() with an inline message.
Drop the per-card stamp on state and sport pages where the place is already the page subject.

Today all three print 'Last checked <date>' beside 'Not yet verified', and 'no date yet' on 236 rows.
reasoning:
My lens: brand, honesty, accessibility and buildability. I scanned all three with axe-core through Playwright (WCAG 2A/2AA/2.1AA/2.2AA, 31 routes at 390px and 1440px), checked the rendered text for dashes, phone numbers, email addresses, money asks, missing-date wording and national counts, read the near/placement code, and looked at the screenshots.

No concept breaks the hard privacy or money rules. All three are clean on email, phone, score, type field and donate. All three also share the same date gap: 'Not yet verified' next to 'Last checked <date>' (which is the automatic crawl date), and 'no date yet' on rows without lastChecked. That needs listedAt added to /api/directory and is not a design difference.

Gallery has the best accessibility (0 axe violations) and the tightest brand use. But it has no skip link, no h1 on the sport, state and grants views (the SEO pages), and query-style hash routes. Its copy says 'who checked it', it rewrites program names while leaving em dashes in grant names, and its placement regex is so strict it discards real cities.

Near You has the most complete honest place logic and the only real map. But it fails contrast badly on its tile maps (2.61:1 and 2.91:1, with 9-12px text). Its floating Map pill hides the date on phone cards, two-column cards cut off the city we are only allowed to show, it has no focus trap, and it has the loosest type and radius system.

Clubhouse wins on my lens because it is closest to production. Its routes already copy the real paths, and one community template renders sport, state, grants and events, which matches the Worker's server-rendered model and gives one page per sport and per state. Its tokens follow the manual's radius scale and font stack, its compact rows keep pages light, and it has a skip link and a focus trap. Its 4 axe failures are mechanical one-line fixes. Its real faults are voice and copy: national counts, letter promises the backend cannot keep, a word-match 'In Tampa', and an unfiltered Grants tab. All are cheap to fix.

The winner should take Near You's map, city parser and state header, and Gallery's share poster (as og:image), its home-page place plates and its accessibility patterns.
